scenario: Greeting someone for the first time

dialogue.translation: Are you from here? I live in the market near the water house.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ah, m nà-emesị n'ụlọ mmiri nke à, kwanu?
dialogue.translation: Ah, I live in that water house too, right?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ee, m nọ n'ụlọ nke n'azụ ọrịa ike.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I live in the house behind the tall person.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ọ di mma, anyị nọ n'ụlọ nà ọzọ.
dialogue.translation: That’s great, we live in that same house.

scenario: Asking the time on the street

refers to a day or days
used here in the sense of 'to be open'
used here in the sense of 'to operate' or 'to run'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Kedu ụbọchị na-e kpọ n'ụlọ ndoro ndoro?
dialogue.translation: How many days are you open per week?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A kpọ na-aga nke 6 n'ụbọchị nke izu.
dialogue.translation: We are open for 6 days in a week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọgụgụ ọjọụụ na-e kpọ banyere?
dialogue.translation: What time are you open on Sunday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ụlọ ndoro ndoro lụ ga-e kpọ na 8am - 6pm.
dialogue.translation: We will be open from 8am to 6pm.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gịnị? Ị ga-e kpọ n'ụzọ ụtọ n'oge ndoro ndoro?
dialogue.translation: Really? You are open late at night?

key_phrases.translation: How many days are you open per week?

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Igbo

vocabulary.note: used to express desire for something
used to describe state or condition

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọ dị mma, biko chọọ ịchọrọ ọrịa dị ugwu?
dialogue.translation: It's good, please tell me what food you want?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ọ dị mma, m chọrọ ọrịa dị ugwu, anị ọsọ.
dialogue.translation: It's good, I want heavy food, also soup.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọ dị mma. Gịnị ka ị gụ akwụkwọ menu?
dialogue.translation: It's good. What do you read on the menu?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: M hụrụ ọsọ mmadụ dị iche iche anị ịgba.
dialogue.translation: I see different soups and I can choose.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọ dị mma, m ga-ịnyere ọrịa dị ugwu anị ọsọ.
dialogue.translation: It's good, I will give you heavy food and soup.

key_phrases.translation: It's good, please tell me...
I want heavy food

key_phrases.phrase: Gịnị ka ị gụ akwụkwọ menu?
key_phrases.translation: What do you read on the menu?

key_phrases.phrase: M ga-ịnyere ọrịa dị ugwu anị ọsọ
key_phrases.translation: I will give you heavy food and soup

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Igbo

vocabulary.note: Refers to a physical location or spot
Can refer to a building or home
Used to connect phrases or clauses

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: M ga-achọrọ ịgba ego n'ọnọdụ a.
dialogue.translation: I want to transfer money at this position.

dialogue.speaker: Bank Teller
dialogue.text: Ọ dị mma, mụta ụlọ ogologo n'ọnọdụ ọnwanyi nke a.
dialogue.translation: It's fine, go to the tall building at the woman's position there.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Ọ di iche? M ga-ịzụ ego m n'ụlọ ogologo nke a.
dialogue.translation: Is that correct? I will take my money to this tall building.

dialogue.speaker: Bank Teller
dialogue.text: Ee, ọ di. Ị ga-achọpụta ego gị n'ọnọdụ a.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it is. You will collect your money at this position.

key_phrases.phrase: M ga-achọrọ ịgba ego n'ọnọdụ a.
key_phrases.translation: I want to transfer money at this position.

key_phrases.phrase: Mụta ụlọ ogologo n'ọnọdụ ọnwanyi nke a.
key_phrases.translation: Go to the tall building at the woman's position there.

key_phrases.phrase: M ga-ịzụ ego m n'ụlọ ogologo nke a.
key_phrases.translation: I will take my money to this tall building.
